title: Can another region be rebuilt?
hook: Two donor regions offer a counterfactual. Which weights match the past?

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: weight donor regions until their blend tracks the treated region before treatment.

misconception: Treating build a synthetic control as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: weight donor regions until their blend tracks the treated region before treatment.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: A treated region goes 10→14 before policy and reaches 25 afterward. Donors A go 8→12→16 and B go 12→16→20. What post-policy gap does their equal-weight blend imply?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-build-a-synthetic-control/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Treated region pre outcomes [10,14], post 25. Donor A [8,12,16], donor B [12,16,20]. Weights .5/.5 reproduce [10,14] and predict 18; post gap 7. Wrong weight .75/.25 produces pre [9,13], post 17.

claims.text: The equal blend retains a post-policy value of 18 and gap 7. Changing donor weights gives 17 and gap 8, while worsening the pre-policy match.

claims.text: A good pre-policy fit constrains the counterfactual. The gap is causal only if the untreated blend would keep tracking the treated region and no other treated-only shock intervenes.

claims.text: A matched donor blend predicts 30 after policy; the treated unit reaches 34. What is the estimated gap? The observed-minus-counterfactual gap is 34−30=4; causal interpretation still needs the design assumptions.
